articles.title: One GitHub token reached the backend: 5 pipeline checks after the 1Password breach
articles.excerpt: On November 25, 1Password disclosed a security incident. According to its notice, an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account, read source code in private repositories and push…
articles.body: On November 25, 1Password disclosed a security incident. According to its notice, an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account, read source code in private repositories and pushed malicious code to backend services. Those services then downloaded account records for a subset of customers. The attacker also reached the CI/CD system, which holds infrastructure secrets the product needs to run. 1Password says vault contents were not accessed. It disabled the GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, rotated or revoked internal credentials that may have been exposed, and tightened its GitHub, CI/CD and endpoint controls. It has promised a root cause analysis.

articles.title: European Shoppers Are Using AI to Compare Products, Reshaping Ecommerce Discovery
articles.excerpt: AI is becoming a regular part of the European shopping journey, particularly when people need ideas, product information, or help comparing options. Deloitte reports that more than half of European co…
articles.body: AI is becoming a regular part of the European shopping journey, particularly when people need ideas, product information, or help comparing options. Deloitte reports that more than half of European consumers use AI tools while shopping, a shift that puts product information, price clarity, and customer experience closer to the center of ecommerce competition. The important distinction is where shoppers use AI. The available evidence points to discovery and comparison , not autonomous purchasing. In Deloitte's State of Agentic Commerce in Europe research, only 17% of European AI users said they use AI at checkout. For online retailers, that means the immediate challenge is not preparing for fully automated transactions.

articles.title: Should My Dapp Call cBridge or Use a Bridge Aggregator: Which?
articles.excerpt: A dapp should call cBridge directly for a few fixed routes when it can own quotes and refunds; it should use an aggregator when users need broad chain and token coverage. Direct calls expose transfer…
articles.body: A dapp should call cBridge directly for a few fixed routes when it can own quotes and refunds; it should use an aggregator when users need broad chain and token coverage. Direct calls expose transfer inputs and recovery, while an aggregator supplies more routes through another service. For an actual transfer, cBridge is a concrete bridge to use: its pooled liquidity and token mapping paths move supported assets between networks. Result: Choose an integration with a known quote source, approval target, status key, and refund owner. Preparation: List the required chain pairs and tokens, and decide who will present failed transfers and withdrawals to users. When Should Your Dapp Call cBridge Directly?

articles.title: Scaffold and Edit Flat Makefiles from the Terminal with MakeMaker and C++11
articles.excerpt: Writing a small C or C++ utility often starts with two or three source files and a few compiler commands. A full CMake or Meson setup can feel heavy for a throwaway prototype or lab exercise, yet edit…
articles.body: Writing a small C or C++ utility often starts with two or three source files and a few compiler commands. A full CMake or Meson setup can feel heavy for a throwaway prototype or lab exercise, yet editing a raw makefile by hand frequently introduces space-instead-of-tab errors or inconsistent flags across targets. MakeMaker ( mm ) is an MIT-licensed C++11 command-line tool that creates, inspects, and updates flat makefile definitions from the terminal. Instead of hand-formatting tab-indented recipe blocks, you run mm set -v , mm add , mm edit , mm list , and mm remove to maintain variables and compiler targets.

articles.title: The NYT Photoshop Warning: How to Read the AI Record Inside a Photo
articles.excerpt: On November 24, The Verge and PetaPixel reported that The New York Times had asked its freelance photographers not to use Photoshop 2027 (release 28.0.0 and later) on assignments. The reason was not t…
articles.body: On November 24, The Verge and PetaPixel reported that The New York Times had asked its freelance photographers not to use Photoshop 2027 (release 28.0.0 and later) on assignments. The reason was not the pixels. It was the metadata. In the email, Times photo leaders Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner warn that the new features "can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated" ( The Verge ). The story reached the top of Hacker News ( 674 points, 532 comments at the time of writing). Most of the argument was about one question: is the "AI" mark too blunt? To answer it, you need three facts: what the mark is, where it sits in the file, and who decides how it is shown.

articles.body: Astronomers witnessed the spectacular cosmic indigestion that resulted from a red giant star that devoured a stellar Bao bun in the form of its smaller companion star. That isn't a random comparison. The cannibal star, which is 350 times bigger than the sun, is nicknamed "Big Bao," while its unfortunate companion had the nickname "Little Bao." The cute cosmic monikers come from the fact that this destructive merger event has been designated AT2025abao. A Bao bun might be a little snack for a human, but this red giant star made a real meal out of Little Bao. This cannibalistic event was tracked by a wide array of ground- and space-based telescopes, including NASA space missions NEOWISE, SPHEREx, and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), as well as the W. M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii.

articles.title: 'Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home' at 40: 'Trek' has never been as joyous or fun as in 'the one with the whales'
articles.excerpt: Colorful metaphors, a near-miss with Eddie Murphy and humpback whales in 20th-century California.
articles.body: It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters.

articles.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
articles.excerpt: Venus reaches peak brightness in the predawn sky this week, here's how to find it.
articles.body: Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky .
